analysis:
The changes are comment-only in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (lines 201-204) and EngineV2KVSizing.swift (lines 8-10). The two test-side changes update expectations: SegmentedProductionGrantTests.swift lines 82-84 and SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift lines 45-48. The GPT-OSS fixture now assumes bf16 K/V on all 24 layers, replacing the earlier bf16 first layer and fp32 for the rest. No executable production code, including nativeKVBytesPerToken, changes in the supplied diff. I found no change to encryption, attestation, the coordinator/provider protocol, authorization, the prefix-cache crypto (T-041), or the fan helper.

The comments refer to EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken, which prices the observed native per-layer types. That file is not in this batch, so I could not verify it. If the production path really charges per-layer observed dtypes, KV accounting is accurate. If a caller still used the fallback, nativeKVBytesPerToken would over-reserve for bf16 rows. That is conservative and fail-safe for availability and memory exhaustion, not an under-reservation. An integration pass should confirm that slotKVBytesPerToken uses observed dtypes and that the fixture's bf16 assumption matches the real SDK. If the real model produced fp32 rows while admission assumed bf16, the pool could be under-accounted. That would be a DoS/memory-pressure risk (T-016 / T-029 class), and it is not demonstrable from this evidence. No findings.
